mcp.note: REAL, not a scaffold — this repo IS an MCP bridge: a Figma plugin (manifest.json, editorType figma/figjam) talking to a localhost MCP server over bridge-server.js. Outstanding for mcp-maintainer: (1) fuzex-figma-bridge still has no tools.json declaring its surface or `mutates` per tool — the plugin protocol in code.js handles start-server/stop-server/mcp-request/client-connect/client-disconnect/get-server-status/ping, which is transport, not a tool manifest; (2) mcp-server-config.json hardcodes an absolute Windows cwd (C:/Users/izzyw/source/FuzeX) so the config is not portable to any other machine or to CI. The second server, design-frames-service, DOES declare tools.json with `mutates` per tool (services/design-frames-service/mcp/tools.json) — added together with the service in the navigable-frames extraction; see services/design-frames-service/docs/EXTRACTION.md.

a2a.note: Reconciled against governance/a2a-runtime-standard.md by a2a-maintainer (gate_a2a.py --all): (1) agent-templates/roles/design-review/role.json's hand-authored `card` object was drift (§4 — never read by card_generator.py) and has been removed; the file now schema-validates and carries a real `skills: [ui-frame-contract, design-system-conformance]` bundle list (previously vacuous, gate-a2a S3) plus a2a.examples/tags for card-projection discoverability. (2) FuzeX now ships its OWN single-tenant A2A pod (deploy/helm/fuzex/templates/a2a.yaml + the a2a/a2aDeploy blocks in values.yaml) — FuzeX is a leaf per FuzeSDLC governance/a2a-dependency-graph.json, not a tenant of FuzeAgent's shared server. Chart-level `a2a.enabled` stays false pending an `a2a-provider-anthropic` SealedSecret (devops-engineer/operator) — flipping it without that secret starts a pod with no provider credential. `providesTo: [FuzeFront]` (below) is the authoritative A2A caller allowlist and was left as-is: it predates this reconciliation as a deliberate grant made when design-frames-service was extracted from FuzeFront (commit 6006b30), which the dependency graph's proposed `providesTo: []` default does not supersede. KNOWN GATE BUG, not a real defect: gate_a2a.py's SHARED_IMAGE constant still reads `ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzeagent-a2a`; that image has been dead since 2026-08-24. The actually-published, actively-updated shared runtime — confirmed against FuzeAgent's own release.yml, its a2a-shared chart, AND the frozen values-interface.schema.json's own `image.repository` default — is `ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuze-a2a`, which this chart correctly uses; the gate's I1 finding against it is the stale artifact (tracked FuzeAgent PR #257), not this repo's config.

portal.reason: FuzeX itself (the Figma/FigJam plugin) still does not register — its UI runs in Figma's plugin sandbox with networkAccess restricted to localhost, so there is no served origin to iframe and no remoteEntry to federate; that part of this note is unchanged. But design-frames-service, its separate network-reachable product surface, now ALSO ships a Module-Federation remote (services/design-frames-service/webapp) reproducing its review UI in React on @izzywdev/fuzefront-design-system — exposed as scope `fuzex`, module `./DesignFramesApp`, served same-origin under /apps/fuzex/remoteEntry.js via the host's reverse proxy, sharing the host's React 19 singleton (NOT an iframe/spa tile). It registers as a portal tile the FuzeFront host mounts directly; the service's REST API (features/flows/frames, openapi.yaml) is unchanged and still consumed over same-origin fetch by that remote. Registration in the app-registry manifest and the reverse-proxy wiring are handled by the orchestrator, not this repo.

identity.note: Declared together with packages/identity/ (governance/identifier-standard.md #2 — each repo keeps its own registry). design-frames-service's Postgres lifecycle tier (services/design-frames-service/docs/postgres-tier.md) mints project/feature/flow/frameRef/approval/discussion/comment ids under this namespace. @izzywdev/fuzefront-identity was checked first: it 401'd under this session's GITHUB_TOKEN scope, and independent of that its ENTITY_PREFIXES registry is a closed literal that cannot be extended from a consuming repo — which the standard says is expected (each repo's own registry, not a central one), so packages/identity/ is the intended permanent home, not a stopgap.
